newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH '97 WHOLESALES, RETAIL SALES SEEN UP 5 PCT.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH '97 WHOLESALES, RETAIL SALES SEEN UP 5 PCT.

text.p: The value of wholesales rose 2.7 percent year-on-year in the first quarter and the value of retail sales including cars rose 4.8 percent, the Federation of Commerce and Trade (KKL) said in a statement on Thursday.
A survey of its members showed expectations of a five percent increase in value of full-year 1997 wholesales and retail sales, it said.

In 1996, the value of KKL members' wholesales rose 5.3 percent year-on-year to 109.91 billion markka, and the value of KKL members' retail sales rose 4.1 percent to 117.95 billion markka, the federation said.
The value of wholesales of cars rose 11.6 percent in January-March. The outlook for full-year 1997 car wholesales was for an increase of 6-9 percent.
Consumer goods wholesales increased 3.1 percent in Q1 and KKL members forecast a full-year rise of 4-6 percent.
Technical goods wholesales declined 1.7 percent in the first three months, but were seen increasing 4-6 percent this year.
In retailing, grocery sales rose 3.6 percent in Q1 and KKL members forecast a full-year 1997 increase in value of 3-5 percent, the federation said.
Department store sales also rose 3.6 percent in January-March and were expected to increase 3-5 percent this year.
Retail sales of cars rose eight percent in the first quarter and were forecast to rise 10-15 percent for the full year, KKL said.
